newsitem.title: USA: Two acquitted in death of Philadelphia jogger.
newsitem.headline: Two acquitted in death of Philadelphia jogger.

text.p: Two men, who claimed police coerced them into signing confessions to a murder they did not commit, were acquitted on Friday on charges of raping and murdering a 26-year-old woman jogger.
After contentious deliberations over two days, a jury found Richard Wise, 20, and Herbert Haak, 26, innocent of all charges, despite alleged confessions by the two men.
In a 3 1/2 week trial, prosecutors charged that Haak and Wise killed the 26-year-old woman, paralegal Kimberly Ernest, as she jogged by while they were breaking into a parked car.

Prosecutors said Ernest died from manual strangulation and accused the pair of leaving her battered body in a stairwell on Nov. 2, 1995. The defence argued that there was no physical evidence linking the two men to the crime and that semen found in the victim did not match the DNA of either defendant.
The two men were arrested when Haak called police to implicate Wise, with whom he shared living quarters.
Haak's signed statement said he accompanied Wise, who hit Ernest with a crowbar and then sexually assaulted her. Wise in his statement admitted assaulting the woman but denied killing her.
But defence lawyers claimed police investigators -- under heavy pressure to solve a high-profile case -- coerced the statements from the two suspects.
Haak testified he was beaten and ordered to sign blank papers but later acknowledged he was unsure of what he was signing. He said he lied in implicating Wise.
Wise's lawyer also said his client was tricked into signing what he thought was a general statement about his background.
